mainTopic: Eggs and offspring of a טרפה: two versions of אמימר's ruling (זה וזה גורם, or whether a טרפה can reproduce), and how long a doubtful טרפה stays forbidden
overview: אמימר rules that eggs already inside a hen when she became a טרפה are forbidden. Eggs formed later come from a forbidden hen and a kosher rooster, so they are permitted under זה וזה גורם מותר. The גמרא defends this ruling from a משנה that forbids a טרפה's egg, and from the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about bringing a טרפה's offspring on the מזבח. In this version they argue about זה וזה גורם. They argue about the מזבח because showing the strength of a lenient view is preferred. This is רב אחא's version, which follows רב אחא בר יעקב that a טרפה can produce offspring. רבינא holds that a טרפה cannot lay eggs or become pregnant. So he teaches אמימר's ruling differently: the first eggs of a doubtful טרפה are permitted only if the bird lays again. In his version the משנה is read as 'finished,' and the offspring dispute is about whether a fetus is part of its mother. The גמרא then rules that a doubtful טרפה is cleared once a male lives twelve months or a female gives birth. It also brings רב הונא's rule that a boneless creature cannot live twelve months, which רב פפא starts to apply to wormy melons, a point that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First clutch forbidden, later eggs permitted
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that eggs already inside the hen when it became a טרפה are forbidden. Eggs formed afterward are permitted because of זה וזה גורם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first batch of eggs is forbidden. From then on, the egg has two causes (the טרפה hen and the kosher rooster), and it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר gives his ruling about the eggs of a hen that became a טרפה. He splits them into eggs that were already there and eggs formed later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clutch was already part of the hen's body when she became a טרפה, so those eggs became forbidden together with her. A later egg comes from two sources, the forbidden hen and the permitted rooster. When a permitted cause and a forbidden cause work together, the result is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clutch: the eggs already inside the hen when she became a טרפה
An animal or bird with a fatal defect, which is forbidden to eat
'This and that cause it': a result produced by both a forbidden and a permitted cause together
From here on; from this point forward

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole rest of the sugya tests this one ruling. It relies on the principle זה וזה גורם מותר.

phrases.english: The first clutch is forbidden,
phrases.notes: The first clutch means the eggs that were already forming inside the hen when she became a טרפה.

phrases.english: from here onward –

phrases.aramaic: הָוֵה לֵיהּ זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם, וּמוּתָּר.
phrases.english: it is a case of 'this and that cause it,' and it is permitted.
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means the טרפה hen and the kosher rooster, which together produce the egg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אמימר's ruling from the previous daf about a hen that became a טרפה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first clutch is forbidden; eggs formed later are permitted because זה וזה גורם מותר.

steps.title: Challenge from the egg of a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר from a משנה that says everyone agrees the egg of a טרפה is forbidden, because it grew in prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenged אמימר: 'And all agree that the egg of a טרפה is forbidden, because it grew in prohibition!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי quotes a משנה that seems to forbid every egg of a טרפה. That contradicts אמימר's ruling that later eggs are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives no exception for eggs formed after the hen became a טרפה. It just says 'it grew in prohibition,' which sounds like any egg growing inside a טרפה is forbidden. That seems to reject אמימר's split between the first clutch and later eggs.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they agree': everyone agrees on this point
The egg of a טרפה bird
It grew while in a forbidden state

phrases.english: Rav Ashi raised an objection to Ameimar:
And they agree regarding the egg of a tereifa that it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in עדיות 5:1.

phrases.english: because it grew in prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אמימר's ruling in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that eggs formed after the hen became a טרפה are permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids the egg of a טרפה with no exception, which seems to include later eggs.

steps.title: The משנה means an egg made without a rooster
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that the משנה is talking about an egg formed without any rooster, so only the טרפה hen caused it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about one warmed from the ground (an egg formed with no rooster).
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers the challenge by limiting the משנה to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no rooster was involved, the egg has only one cause: the forbidden hen. Then זה וזה גורם does not apply, so the egg is forbidden. אמימר's rule still stands for eggs fertilized by a kosher rooster.

keyTerms.meaning: There: in that source
Warmed from the ground: an egg formed without a male

phrases.english: There, it is with one warmed from the ground.
phrases.notes: He means a hen whose egg formed with no rooster at all, so only the forbidden hen produced it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids every egg of a טרפה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only means an egg formed without a rooster, which has a single forbidden cause

steps.title: Why not say the משנה means the first clutch?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אמימר did not give an easier answer: that the משנה means the first clutch, which he already agrees is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him answer that it is talking about the first clutch!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions אמימר's answer. It points to a simpler answer he could have given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר already said the first clutch is forbidden. Reading the משנה as being about those eggs would fit his ruling without inventing an unusual case of an egg with no rooster.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him answer it (this way instead)

phrases.english: And let him answer it as referring to the first clutch?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the answer in step 3 was chosen
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's choice of answer in step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler answer was available, so why choose the unusual case of an egg made without a rooster?

steps.title: The word 'grew' rules out the first clutch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the משנה's wording. For the first clutch it would have said 'was finished' in prohibition, not 'grew' in prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'grew'? It should have said 'was finished'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the first-clutch answer does not work. The wording of the משנה does not fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first-clutch eggs started forming while the hen was still kosher and were only completed after she became a טרפה. That would be described as 'finished in prohibition.' The word 'grew' means the egg's whole growth took place in prohibition, so the משנה must mean a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
It was finished or completed
It should have said

phrases.english: If so, "it grew"?
It should have said "it was finished."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן גָּדְלָה גָּמְרָה מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the source's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could be about the first clutch
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Grew' means the egg's whole growth was in prohibition, so it is not the first clutch
steps.whatToRemember: אמימר survives the challenge: the משנה forbidding a טרפה's egg is about an egg formed with no rooster, as its wording 'grew' shows.

steps.title: The dispute about offspring of a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a source: רבי אליעזר says the offspring of a טרפה may not be brought on the מזבח, and רבי יהושע says it may.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about what we learned: The offspring of a טרפה: רבי אליעזר says it may not be offered on the altar, and רבי יהושע says it may be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to set up its next question. It does not challenge anything yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source is about animals, not eggs. The question is whether a calf born to a טרפה mother counts as fit for the מזבח. The גמרא will next ask what case this argument is about.

keyTerms.meaning: But then; introduces a new difficulty
The offspring of a טרפה animal
It may be offered as a קרבן
The altar

phrases.english: But then, that which we learned:
The offspring of a tereifa – Rabbi Eliezer says:
it may not be offered on the altar,
and Rabbi Yehoshua says: it may be offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source that tests the rule of זה וזה גורם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the offspring of a טרפה may not be offered; רבי יהושע: it may.

steps.title: What case are they arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what are they arguing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact case and reason behind the argument. This prepares the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the גמרא can use this source, it has to know which situation the two תנאים are talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case behind the dispute in step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The case and reasoning behind the dispute about the offspring of a טרפה

steps.title: They argue about זה וזה גורם
steps.stepSummary: The suggested answer: the mother became a טרפה and only then became pregnant from a kosher male. רבי אליעזר holds זה וזה גורם is forbidden, and רבי יהושע holds it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where she became a טרפה and afterward became pregnant. רבי אליעזר holds that 'this and that cause it' is forbidden, and רבי יהושע holds that 'this and that cause it' is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the argument is about the rule זה וזה גורם, the same rule אמימר used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the pregnancy started after she became a טרפה, the calf comes from a forbidden mother and a kosher father. So the argument becomes a clash over whether such a mixed cause is permitted. This would make רבי יהושע support אמימר.

keyTerms.meaning: She became a טרפה and only afterward became pregnant
He holds (this view)

phrases.english: Where she became a tereifa and afterward became pregnant,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם אָסוּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds: 'this and that cause it' is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua holds: 'this and that cause it' is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a mother who became a טרפה before becoming pregnant, and they argue whether זה וזה גורם is forbidden or permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: The next line challenges this explanation, but the גמרא defends it in steps 10 and 12. Step 13 then builds on it, so in this version it stays as the explanation of the dispute.

steps.title: Why argue about the מזבח and not about eating?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the explanation: if they argue about זה וזה גורם, why frame it around the מזבח instead of whether an ordinary person may eat it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, instead of arguing about the Most High, let them argue about an ordinary person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from step 8. A dispute about זה וזה גורם should show up first in the plain question of eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument were about זה וזה גורם, the basic question would be whether the offspring may be eaten at all. The fact that they only discuss the מזבח suggests their argument is about something specific to קרבנות, not about זה וזה גורם.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
'The Most High': things offered to ה׳ on the מזבח
An ordinary person: here, regular eating

phrases.english: If so, rather than disputing regarding the Most High,
phrases.notes: 'The Most High' means bringing the animal as a קרבן on the מזבח.

phrases.english: let them disagree regarding an ordinary person?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אַדְּמִיפַּלְגִי לְגָבוֹהַּ לִיפַּלְגוּ לְהֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about זה וזה גורם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dispute about זה וזה גורם would apply to ordinary eating, so framing it only around the מזבח makes no sense under that explanation.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this challenge held, the dispute could not serve as a source about זה וזה גורם. The גמרא therefore defends the explanation in the next step.

steps.title: The argument is about the altar to show how strong רבי יהושע's leniency is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the dispute is framed around the מזבח to teach that רבי יהושע permits the offspring even as an offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: To teach you the strength of רבי יהושע's view: he permits it even for the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9. It explains why the argument is about the מזבח and not about an ordinary person eating the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהושע permits the offspring even for the מזבח, where the rules are stricter, then he certainly permits an ordinary person to eat it. Framing the argument around the מזבח shows how far his leniency reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'to the Most High'; for the מזבח, as an offering
His strength; how far his opinion goes
Permitted

phrases.english: To let you know the strength of רבי יהושע's view,
that even for the Most High it is also permitted.
phrases.notes: 'The Most High' here means bringing it as an offering on the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the framing as a way to show how far the lenient view reaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Framing the argument around the מזבח suggests it is not about זה וזה גורם
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about זה וזה גורם; the מזבח framing shows that רבי יהושע permits it even for offerings

steps.title: Why not argue about an ordinary person to show רבי אליעזר's strictness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: they could have argued about an ordinary person, which would show that רבי אליעזר forbids it even for regular eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them argue about an ordinary person, to teach you the strength of רבי אליעזר's view, that he forbids it even to an ordinary person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 10. If the point is to show the strength of a view, the other side could have been shown just as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Arguing about an ordinary person would show that רבי אליעזר forbids the animal even for regular eating, which is less strict than the מזבח. So why choose to show רבי יהושע's strength and not רבי אליעזר's?

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person, as opposed to the מזבח
And let them argue
Forbidden

phrases.english: But let them argue about an ordinary person,
to let you know the strength of רבי אליעזר's view,
that even for an ordinary person it is also forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the מזבח framing is meant to show רבי יהושע's strength
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reasoning could support the opposite framing, showing רבי אליעזר's strength instead

steps.title: Showing the strength of a leniency is preferred
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is better to show how far a lenient view goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The strength of permitting is preferred by him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 11 briefly. The תנא prefers to show the strength of the lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone can be strict out of doubt, so a strict ruling does not prove much. A lenient ruling shows real confidence in the law, so it is more worth teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The strength of a leniency is preferred; it is better to show how far a lenient view goes

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule of thumb in the גמרא for why a dispute is framed in one direction and not the other.

phrases.english: The strength of permitting is preferred by him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the תנא who framed the argument this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general principle of teaching style
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both framings are equally good, so choosing the מזבח needs a reason
steps.terutzMaskana: Showing the reach of a leniency is preferred, so the מזבח framing was chosen

steps.title: The forbidden טרפה egg is one laid without a male
steps.stepSummary: Because they argue about זה וזה גורם, the משנה's agreement that a טרפה's egg is forbidden must refer to an egg with only one cause.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that the egg of a טרפה is forbidden. This is about a bird warmed by the earth, where there is only one cause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion about the משנה's line that everyone agrees a טרפה's egg is forbidden. It explains which kind of egg that line means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument is about two causes, a male and the טרפה mother, then the case everyone forbids must have only one cause. That is an egg the bird produced without a male, so only the טרפה mother caused it.

keyTerms.meaning: They agree
The egg of a טרפה bird
Warmed by the earth; laid without a male
Only one cause

steps.whatToRemember: The argument is about זה וזה גורם. Where only the טרפה is the cause, everyone forbids it.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not say every egg of a טרפה is forbidden. It is only an egg with no male involved, where the טרפה is the only cause.

phrases.english: And they agree about the egg of a טרפה that it is forbidden,
this is where it was warmed by the earth,
phrases.notes: This means a hen that made the egg without any male.

phrases.english: so that it has only one cause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of steps 8 through 12 to define the case in the משנה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The forbidden טרפה egg is one laid without a male, where the טרפה is the only cause

steps.title: רב אחא follows רב אחא בר יעקב and teaches אמימר's statement as said earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב אחא agrees with רב אחא בר יעקב, so he teaches אמימר's statement the way the גמרא said earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא holds like רב אחא בר יעקב, and he teaches אמימר's statement as we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic by placing רב אחא's view. It explains which way he teaches אמימר's statement and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא בר יעקב held that a טרפה can give birth, and so a טרפה bird can lay eggs. Since רב אחא agrees, he teaches אמימר's statement in the version the גמרא gave earlier, that an egg fertilized after the bird became a טרפה is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds this view
As we said earlier

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: רב אחא holds like רב אחא בר יעקב,
and he teaches the statement of אמימר as we said.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the conclusion back to the earlier discussion of אמימר's statement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אחא follows רב אחא בר יעקב that a טרפה can produce offspring, and so teaches אמימר's statement as given earlier

steps.title: רבינא's version of אמימר's ruling on eggs
steps.stepSummary: רבינא does not agree with רב אחא בר יעקב, so he teaches אמימר's ruling another way: hold back the first eggs, and permit them only if the bird lays again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא disagrees with רב אחא בר יעקב, and he teaches אמימר's statement like this: With eggs from a bird that might be a טרפה, we set aside the first clutch. If the bird lays eggs again, those first eggs are permitted. If not, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of אמימר's ruling, taught by רבינא, who disagrees with רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא holds that a real טרפה cannot lay new eggs. So if the bird lays again, that proves it was never a טרפה, and the first eggs are permitted. If it never lays again, we treat it as a טרפה, and the first eggs, which were inside it, are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal or bird that might be a טרפה (fatally injured), but we are not sure
The first clutch (batch) of eggs
We set aside and wait
She lays (literally 'carries') eggs again

steps.confusionAlert: The proof in this version is that a real טרפה cannot lay eggs. So the bird laying again is what shows it was never a טרפה.

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא לָא סָבַר לַהּ כִּדְרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: Ravina does not hold like Rav Acha bar Yaakov,
and he teaches Ameimar's statement in this wording:
Ameimar said:
these eggs of a bird that might be a treifa,
the first clutch, we set them aside and wait,
if she lays again, they are permitted,
and if not, they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא לָא סָבַר לַהּ כִּדְרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other version of אמימר's ruling, set against רב אחא's version in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טרפה cannot lay eggs. The first clutch from a bird that might be a טרפה is permitted only if the bird lays again.

steps.title: רב אשי objects from the משנה about a טרפה's egg
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes the משנה that a טרפה's egg is forbidden because it grew while the bird was forbidden. That suggests a טרפה can produce eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenged אמימר: The משנה says they agree that the egg of a טרפה is forbidden, because it grew while the bird was forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges אמימר's ruling with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'It grew while forbidden' sounds like the egg formed after the bird became a טרפה. That would mean a טרפה can make eggs, which goes against רבינא's version of אמימר.

keyTerms.meaning: The egg of a טרפה bird
It grew while the bird was forbidden
They agree (both sides of the dispute)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi challenged Ameimar:
"And they agree about the egg of a treifa that it is forbidden,
because it grew while forbidden."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's version of אמימר, that a טרפה cannot lay eggs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's words 'it grew while forbidden' suggest the egg formed after the bird became a טרפה.

steps.title: The משנה means the first clutch
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that the משנה is talking about the first clutch, the eggs already inside the bird when it became a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said to him: There the משנה is talking about the first clutch.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers רב אשי's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden egg in the משנה was not made by a טרפה. It was already forming before the injury and was finished after it. So the משנה does not prove that a טרפה can make new eggs.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There it is about the first clutch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case (אוקימתא) to the first clutch
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's egg was made after the bird became a טרפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's egg was already in the bird before it became a טרפה.

steps.title: Then the משנה should say 'finished'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי pushes back: if the egg was already forming before the injury, the משנה should say it was 'finished' while forbidden, not that it 'grew' while forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'it grew'? It should have said 'it was finished'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges אמימר's answer based on the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Grew' sounds like the whole egg developed while the bird was a טרפה. If the egg only got completed after the injury, the right word would be 'finished.'

keyTerms.meaning: It was finished (completed)
It should have said

phrases.english: If so, "it grew"?
It should have said "it was finished"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's reading that the משנה means the first clutch
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'grew' does not fit an egg that was only completed after the injury.

steps.title: Change the wording to 'finished'
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that we should read the משנה with the word 'finished.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: 'it was finished.'
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers by changing the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the משנה reads 'it was finished while forbidden,' it clearly fits the first clutch. The challenge falls away, and רבינא's view that a טרפה cannot lay eggs stands.

phrases.english: Teach: "it was finished."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says 'grew,' which suggests a טרפה makes eggs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה should say 'finished,' which fits the first clutch.

steps.title: What about the dispute over a טרפה's offspring?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings up the dispute about the offspring of a טרפה. If a טרפה cannot become pregnant, what case are they arguing about?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the source we learned: about the offspring of a טרפה, רבי אליעזר says it may not be offered on the מזבח, and רבי יהושע says it may be offered. What are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge: if a טרפה cannot give birth, the dispute about a טרפה's offspring needs explaining. This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב אחא's version, they argued about זה וזה גורם (step 8). That reading assumed a טרפה can conceive. Under רבינא's view it cannot, so the גמרא must find another case for the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: The offspring (baby animal) of a טרפה
It may not be offered on the altar
What are they arguing about?

phrases.english: But that which we learned:
"The offspring of a treifa,

phrases.aramaic: ר׳ אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא יִקְרַב לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: it may not be offered on the altar,
Rabbi Yehoshua says: it may be offered";
what are they arguing about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the egg challenge is answered, a second source is raised against the view that a טרפה cannot reproduce.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's view that a טרפה cannot become pregnant
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dispute about a טרפה's offspring seems to assume a טרפה can give birth.

steps.title: Pregnant first, טרפה later
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is about an animal that became pregnant first and only later became a טרפה. They argue whether a fetus counts as part of its mother's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about a case where the mother became pregnant and only later became a טרפה. רבי אליעזר holds a fetus is like its mother's thigh. רבי יהושע holds a fetus is not like its mother's thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the dispute in a way that fits רבינא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby was formed while the mother was healthy, so we never need a טרפה to get pregnant. רבי אליעזר says the fetus is part of the mother, so it became a טרפה along with her. רבי יהושע says it is a separate body, so it stays fine.

keyTerms.meaning: She became pregnant and afterward became a טרפה
A fetus is like its mother's thigh, a part of her body

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different explanation of the same dispute than in step 8 (זה וזה גורם). Each explanation fits a different view of whether a טרפה can get pregnant.

phrases.english: When she became pregnant and afterward became a treifa,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: עוּבָּר יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds: a fetus is its mother's thigh,
phrases.notes: He means the fetus is treated like a limb of the mother, so whatever happens to her happens to it.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר: עוּבָּר לָאו יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua holds: a fetus is not its mother's thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case (אוקימתא): pregnancy came before the injury
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute requires a טרפה that became pregnant.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mother was pregnant before becoming a טרפה. The dispute is whether the fetus counts as part of the mother.

steps.title: Why argue about the altar and not ordinary eating?
steps.stepSummary: If they argue about whether the fetus is part of its mother, the bigger question is whether a regular person may even eat it. Why argue only about the מזבח?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, instead of arguing about offering it to the Most High, let them argue about an ordinary person eating it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי אליעזר, the fetus would be a טרפה itself and forbidden to anyone. So the dispute would apply to plain eating, not just to the מזבח. This repeats the question from step 9, now in רבינא's version.

keyTerms.meaning: The Most High, meaning offerings on the מזבח
An ordinary person, meaning regular eating

phrases.english: If so,
instead of arguing about the Most High,
let them argue about an ordinary person!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אַדְּמִיפַּלְגִי לְגָבוֹהַּ, לִיפַּלְגוּ לְהֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: Framing the dispute around the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the fetus is a טרפה in רבי אליעזר's view, it is forbidden even for ordinary eating, so the dispute should be framed that way.

steps.title: To show how far רבי יהושע goes
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is framed around the מזבח to show that רבי יהושע permits the offspring even as an offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is to show you the strength of רבי יהושע's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מזבח framing shows how far רבי יהושע's lenient view reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהושע allows the offspring even on the מזבח, where the rules are stricter, he obviously allows it for ordinary eating. The same answer was given in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: To show you the strength (how far) of his view

phrases.english: To show you the strength of Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the משנה chose this framing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ordinary-eating case is the natural one to argue about.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מזבח case shows that רבי יהושע permits even there.

steps.title: Why not show how far רבי אליעזר goes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: they could have argued about ordinary eating, to show that רבי אליעזר forbids it even then.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them argue about an ordinary person, to show you the strength of רבי אליעזר's view!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer: the other framing would show how far the strict view goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Framing the dispute around ordinary eating would show that רבי אליעזר forbids the offspring even for regular food, not only for the מזבח. So why prefer one framing over the other?

phrases.english: But let them argue about an ordinary person
to show you the strength of Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיפַּלְגוּ בְּהֶדְיוֹט לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה wanted to show רבי יהושע's strength
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Showing רבי אליעזר's strength through the ordinary-eating case would be just as good.

steps.title: Showing leniency is preferred
steps.stepSummary: The תנא prefers to show how far a lenient view goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The strength of a lenient view is preferable to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the back-and-forth: the תנא prefers to highlight how far a lenient view goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone can be strict when unsure. Being lenient requires confidence, so showing the full reach of a lenient view teaches more. That is why the משנה chose the מזבח case.

keyTerms.meaning: The strength of a lenient ruling is preferred

steps.whatToRemember: In רבינא's version, a טרפה cannot lay eggs or get pregnant. The egg in the משנה was 'finished' after the injury, and the offspring dispute is about a mother pregnant before she became a טרפה. The מזבח framing shows how far רבי יהושע's leniency goes.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle כח דהיתירא עדיף comes up across ש״ס to explain why a source picks the case that shows the reach of the lenient view.

phrases.english: The strength of leniency is preferable to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 and closes the discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle about how a תנא chooses examples
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה frames the dispute around the מזבח because showing how far a lenient view reaches is more important.

steps.title: Why even רבי יהושע forbids the egg of a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: Following the explanation from the previous steps, the משנה's statement that everyone forbids the egg of a טרפה bird is about the first clutch of eggs. Those eggs are part of the bird's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they certainly agree that the egg of a טרפה is forbidden. This is talking about the first clutch of eggs. Why? Because the egg is part of the bird's body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies its explanation of the dispute to the last line of the משנה, about the egg of a טרפה bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע held that a fetus is not part of its mother's body. Here the גמרא says an egg is different. Eggs already forming inside the bird when it became a טרפה are truly its body, so even רבי יהושע forbids them.

keyTerms.meaning: The egg of a bird that is a טרפה
The first clutch: eggs already forming inside the bird when it became a טרפה
It is its body, meaning truly part of the mother

steps.whatToRemember: A fetus may be its own thing according to רבי יהושע, but an egg still inside the bird counts as the bird's own body.

phrases.english: And they certainly concede regarding the egg of a tereifa that it is forbidden,
this is with the first clutch [of eggs],
phrases.notes: These are the eggs already forming inside the bird at the moment it became a טרפה.

phrases.english: What is the reason? It is its body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation of the משנה by fitting its last clause into the approach from steps 21-25
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Everyone forbids eggs that were forming when the bird became a טרפה, because an egg is part of the mother's body.

steps.title: The practical rule for an animal that may be a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה for an animal whose טרפה status is in doubt: a male is forbidden for twelve months, and a female until it gives birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: for a male, it stays forbidden for the full twelve months. For a female, it stays forbidden as long as it has not given birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling for an animal we are not sure is a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doubtful animal stays forbidden until it passes a test that shows it is healthy. For a male, the test is living twelve months. For a female, the test is giving birth. After that, we know it was never a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is, introducing the final practical ruling
A male animal
A female animal
Gives birth

steps.whatToRemember: For an animal that may be a טרפה: a male is cleared after twelve months, and a female is cleared once it gives birth.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: with a male,
phrases.notes: This is about an animal we are unsure is a טרפה. Until these milestones pass, it stays forbidden.

phrases.english: [it is forbidden] all twelve months;
with a female, as long as it does not give birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from explaining the משנה to giving a practical halachic ruling about a doubtful טרפה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A doubtful טרפה is permitted after a male lives twelve months or a female gives birth.

steps.title: A boneless creature cannot live twelve months
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא states that any creature without bones cannot survive for twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Any creature that has no bones cannot survive twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a new rule about nature: creatures with no bones do not live a full twelve months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the twelve-month idea from the previous ruling. It is a new fact about living things. The next step will use it to explain a הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A creature or living thing
Bone
Survives or lasts

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:
Any (creature) that has no bone
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: does not survive twelve months.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כֹּל בְּרִיָּה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ עֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, linked to the previous step by the theme of twelve months
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No boneless creature lives for twelve months.

steps.title: רב פפא begins to learn from רב הונא about שמואל's ruling on worms
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that רב הונא's rule teaches us something about שמואל's ruling: worms that grew in a melon while it was still attached to the ground are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We can learn from רב הונא's statement about what שמואל said: A melon that became wormy while still attached to the ground is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא sets up a link between רב הונא's rule and שמואל's ruling about wormy melons. The explanation of what we learn comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל forbids worms that grew in a melon while it was still growing in the ground. רב פפא says רב הונא's rule about boneless creatures will help us understand that ruling. At this point we have only the two statements side by side.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, meaning we can draw a conclusion
A type of long melon or cucumber
Became infested with worms
While still attached to where it grows

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Learn from it, from Rav Huna's statement,
[about] that which Shmuel said:
A melon that became wormy while attached [to the ground] is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the spelling in round brackets; the square brackets give the corrected spelling. The worms are what is forbidden, because they grew while the melon was still in the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב הונא's rule from step 28 to begin explaining שמואל's ruling
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that worms in a melon that became wormy while attached to the ground are forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's rule that boneless creatures do not live twelve months
